project_description: VitaFlow is a zero-dependency, single-file health and wellness toolkit that runs entirely offline in Node.js. It packs six practical health tools behind one command: a meal nutrition analyzer with a 50+ item food database that scales every nutrient by serving weight and compares protein, carbs, fat, fiber, sugar, sodium, vitamin C, calcium and iron against daily reference intakes with progress bars; a BMR/TDEE calculator combining the Mifflin-St Jeor and Revised Harris-Benedict equations with five activity levels and three goals (fat loss, maintenance, lean gain) that outputs calorie and macronutrient targets; a workout plan generator spanning strength, hypertrophy and endurance across 2-6 days, bodyweight/gym/mixed equipment and three experience levels; a guided breathing coach with 4-7-8, box and coherent techniques; a sleep quality analyzer that computes sleep efficiency and a 0-100 score from bed/rise times with actionable improvement tips; and a CSV-driven health trend dashboard tracking weight, steps, sleep, water, energy, stress and mood with automatic insights. A one-command integrated report with built-in demo data showcases the entire flow, and a 34-assertion self-test suite verifies every module. Safety is a first-class concern: every output carries a medical disclaimer, all inputs are range-validated, out-of-range biometrics trigger professional-care recommendations, and no output is ever framed as medical advice. No dependencies, no install, no network required — works on Node 18+ out of the box.
code_note: Zero-dependency CommonJS single file (~50KB, well under the 100KB limit). Node 18+ compatible; verified with node --check and an in-file --self-test that runs 34 assertions covering nutrition scaling, dual-formula BMR, workout plan generation, breathing session timing, sleep efficiency/score, CSV trend analysis, input validation and disclaimer presence. Run: node tool.js --self-test; node tool.js report --demo. All commands also accept real user input via flags. Contains no TODO/FIXME/debugger markers and no require() calls.
